mainTopic: Whose opinion is the משנה about the vow word לחולין? The גמרא tests whether it fits רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה.
overview: The גמרא first assumes that the vow word לחולין means 'not חולין, but a קרבן.' That reading needs the rule that from a negative statement you can hear a positive one (מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן). The גמרא shows it cannot be רבי מאיר, because his rule about the double condition of בני גד ובני ראובן shows he rejects that idea. So the משנה must be רבי יהודה. But the end of the משנה names רבי יהודה, which suggests the beginning belongs to someone else. The גמרא answers that the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and the last clause explains the earlier part instead of arguing with it. Then a ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that 'like ירושלים' is not a vow at all, while our משנה counts it as one. The final answer is that two תנאים reported רבי יהודה's view differently, so the whole משנה can still be his.

steps.title: The starting assumption: לחולין means 'not חולין, but an offering'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by stating how it first understood the vow word לחולין in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: At first they assumed: what does 'לחולין' mean? 'It should not be ordinary (חולין), but rather a קרבן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how it first read the strange vow word לחולין: the person meant 'let this NOT be ordinary food, let it be a קרבן.' This assumption sets up the next question about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סברוה means 'they assumed,' but as תוספות point out, here that understanding is never overturned. It stays in place to the end. On this reading, the person only said something negative ('not חולין'), and we are filling in the positive ('so it is a קרבן'). That gap is exactly what the next steps will test.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'They assumed.' This marks a first understanding that may be changed later
The vow word in the משנה, read here as לא חולין, 'not ordinary'
Ordinary, non-holy food or items
An offering; something holy and forbidden for personal use

steps.confusionAlert: סברוה means 'they assumed.' Whenever you see it, expect that this understanding is only a starting point and may be changed later in the סוגיא.

phrases.notes: They are reading the opening ל of לחולין as if it were the word לא, 'not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's vow word לחולין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the first assumption, לחולין means 'not חולין, but a קרבן,' so the item becomes forbidden like a קרבן.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה? Not רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows and rules out רבי מאיר, who does not infer a positive from a negative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? If you say רבי מאיר, he does not hold that from a negative statement you can hear a positive one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows, given the reading from step 1. It shows that רבי מאיר does not fit, because he does not infer a 'yes' from a 'no.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person only said 'not חולין.' Calling the item a קרבן means hearing a positive ('it IS a קרבן') from a negative. רבי מאיר rejects that kind of inference, so our משנה cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose is our משנה?' It asks which תנא the משנה follows
From a negative statement you can hear a positive one
He does not hold of this idea

phrases.english: he does not hold that from a negative

phrases.notes: Here the negative is 'not חולין,' and the positive we would infer is 'so it is a קרבן.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the reading in step 1 assumes and asks which תנא could hold it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה follows, given that it relies on hearing a positive from a negative.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה could follow רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר does not infer a positive from a negative, yet the משנה does.

steps.title: Proof: רבי מאיר requires a double condition like בני גד ובני ראובן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי מאיר rejects inferring a positive from a negative, using his rule about conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי מאיר says, any condition that is not like the condition of בני גד ובני ראובן is not a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove what it just said about רבי מאיר. He holds that a condition only works if it is spelled out both ways, like משה's deal with בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said both 'if you fight, you get the land' and 'if you don't, you don't.' רבי מאיר requires both sides to be stated, which shows he won't fill in the unspoken side on his own. So for him, 'not חולין' does not automatically mean 'קרבן.'

keyTerms.meaning: A condition
The tribes of גד and ראובן, whose deal with משה is the model for a valid condition

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of תנאי כפול (a double condition) comes from this case, and it shows up all over ש״ס, especially in קידושין and גיטין.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Meir says:
like the condition of the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben —
phrases.notes: במדבר 32:29–30. משה stated both the 'if yes' and the 'if not' sides of the deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2's claim about רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר does not hold מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's rule that only a double condition, like that of בני גד ובני ראובן, is valid.

steps.title: So the משנה must be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Having ruled out רבי מאיר, the גמרא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: since רבי מאיר does not fit, the משנה must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does accept that you can infer a positive from a negative. So he can read 'not חולין' as meaning 'קרבן.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' It swaps in a new answer after the first one fails

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2's question after רבי מאיר was ruled out.

steps.title: Challenge: the end of the משנה names רבי יהודה, so the beginning seems to be someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the last clause of the משנה is attributed to רבי יהודה, which suggests the earlier part is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: רבי יהודה says, one who says 'ירושלים' has said nothing. Since the last clause is רבי יהודה, the first clause is not רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 4. If the משנה names רבי יהודה only at the end, it sounds like the earlier part, which includes לחולין, belongs to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when a משנה names a תנא only at the end, that תנא is disagreeing with what came before. So it seems the first part is not רבי יהודה, and we are back to having no תנא for it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Look at the end clause' of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה
'He has said nothing.' His words are not a vow at all

phrases.english: Say the latter clause: Rabbi Yehuda says:
From the fact that the latter clause is Rabbi Yehuda —
the first clause is not Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 4's answer that the משנה is רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first part of the משנה (לחולין) follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא named only in the last clause usually disagrees with what came before, so the first clause must belong to someone else.

steps.title: Answer: the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and the last clause explains the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה follows רבי יהודה. The last clause is an explanation, not a disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and this is what it teaches: for רבי יהודה says, one who says 'ירושלים' has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the last line as an explanation. It is not a separate opinion, so the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שֶׁ ('for') turns רבי יהודה's line into a reason that adds to the earlier clauses instead of arguing with them. So רבי יהודה, who does infer a positive from a negative, can be the author of the לחולין clause as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'All of it.' The whole משנה
'And this is what it is teaching.' It introduces a re-reading of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The first reading of לחולין ('not חולין, but קרבן') needs מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן. רבי מאיר rejects that rule, so the משנה is assigned to רבי יהודה. The last clause, 'רבי יהודה אומר,' is read as an explanation ('for רבי יהודה says'), so the whole משנה is his.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'רבי יהודה אומר' at the end of a משנה as automatically disagreeing with the earlier part. Here the גמרא reads it as 'for רבי יהודה says,' an explanation within one single opinion.

phrases.english: The entire mishna is Rabbi Yehuda,
and this is what it is teaching:

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5's challenge and confirms step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the משנה: the last clause becomes an explanation instead of a disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last clause's 'רבי יהודה אומר' marks a disagreement, so the first part belongs to another תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה follows רבי יהודה. His line is read as 'for רבי יהודה says' and explains the earlier part.

steps.title: A teaching shows רבי יהודה does not forbid an item called "like ירושלים"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the whole משנה is רבי יהודה. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that a vow of "like ירושלים" has no effect, but the משנה treats it as a valid vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says an item should be "like ירושלים," would רבי יהודה say the item is forbidden? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: someone who says "like ירושלים" has said nothing, unless he vows using something that is actually offered in ירושלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, that the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems to disagree with part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts "like ירושלים" (כירושלים) as a vow that forbids the item. But in the ברייתא, רבי יהודה says that even "like ירושלים" does nothing, unless the vow uses something actually offered there. So it looks like at least that part of the משנה cannot be רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: "Like ירושלים": a vow comparing an item to ירושלים
Is it forbidden? (a challenging question)
Something that is offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying vows connected to ירושלים never work. He says the vow works only when it uses something actually offered there, like a קרבן.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda, is it forbidden?
But it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who says "like Jerusalem" has not said anything,
unless he vows by something that is offered in Jerusalem!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 6's conclusion that the entire משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole משנה, including the vow "like ירושלים," follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying a vow of "like ירושלים" has no effect. The משנה says it does take effect, so the משנה seems not to be רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Two teachers report רבי יהודה's view differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps its position that the whole משנה is רבי יהודה. The משנה and the ברייתא come from two different תנאים, and each reports רבי יהודה's opinion in a different way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה. There are two תנאים who each report what רבי יהודה held, and they report it differently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It does not give up on saying the משנה is רבי יהודה. Instead, it explains that the משנה and the ברייתא are two different reports of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was a clash between two sources that both claim to show רבי יהודה's opinion. The answer is that they are not two opinions of רבי יהודה himself. They are two students or traditions who understood and passed on his view differently. Our משנה follows the version in which "like ירושלים" does count as a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire משנה
Two תנאים, two teachers from the time of the משנה
According to the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: When two sources quote the same תנא differently, the גמרא can answer "two תנאים according to him." The two sources are different reports of his view, so the משנה can still be his.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and there are two tannaim who disagree about Rabbi Yehuda's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וּתְרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two תנאים report רבי יהודה's opinion differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה rejects a vow of "like ירושלים," so the משנה cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only one report of רבי יהודה's view. Our משנה follows another תנא's report, in which the vow does take effect. So the whole משנה is still רבי יהודה.
